question: What Is the Working Principle of a Microcontroller?
body_html:
The microcontroller working principle is a complete small computer on one chip: CPU, Flash or ROM for the program, RAM for temporary data, I/O ports with ADC, timers and serial interfaces (UART, SPI, I2C).

On power up it loads boot code from Flash, initialises the hardware, then runs the main program in a loop, using interrupts so peripherals can call the CPU when needed. A microprocessor, by contrast, needs external memory and I/O chips.
